report.summary: Reviewed killswitch.py chunk 2 of 3: public symbols include marker_path, reason, __repr__, _marker_present, read_state, should_stop, __call__, is_set, wait, checkpoint, track, stop_children, children_stopped, start_watch, stop_watch, _watch_loop, watch, __enter__, __exit__, _atomic_write. All docstring claims checked against code.
risks: _marker_present | low | Uses os.stat instead of Path.exists to avoid swallowing OSError; claim that only FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError mean absent is correct per code, but any other OSError returns True (present) with a reason. This is intentional but could lead to false positives if marker is temporarily inaccessible. | Verify that temporary OSErrors (e.g., permission denied) should indeed be treated as stop.

read_state | medium | The docstring claims 'Every early return below is a STOP. There is exactly one running exit'. Code shows multiple early returns (halt calls) that return stopped=True. The single running exit is at the end. Verified correct.

should_stop | high | Docstring claims 'NEVER raises, and NEVER returns False because something went wrong'. Code catches BaseException to ensure no raise. However, if read_state raises BaseException, it is caught and returns stopped=True. This is correct. But note that the lock acquisition (with self._lock) could theoretically raise (e.g., if lock is broken), but that is not handled. Risk is low but possible.

watch_loop | high | The comment about cooperative_grace_s and the race condition is extensive and references external behavior (pytest_gate, attempt.py). This claim is uncheckable in this chunk. The code does implement the wait and stop_children calls as described.

_atomic_write | medium | Docstring claims it delegates to write_text_atomic from daedalus.atomic. The code calls write_text_atomic(target, text, retry_s=retry_s). This is correct, but the import is not visible in this chunk. Claim that behaviour is unchanged from earlier implementation is uncheckable.

handoff.purpose: KillSwitch class: properties, state reading, latching, children management, watcher loop, atomic write delegation.

symbols.name: _marker_present
symbols.note: Returns tuple (present, unreadable_reason). Uses os.stat to check marker.

symbols.name: read_state
symbols.note: Reads permit from disk, returns SwitchState. Never raises.

symbols.name: should_stop
symbols.note: Returns True once then forever. Latches on first stop.

symbols.name: track
symbols.note: Registers a ManagedProcess for reaping. Returns its argument.

symbols.name: stop_children
symbols.note: Cancels tracked trees and optionally sweeps managed processes.

symbols.name: start_watch
symbols.note: Starts daemon thread for polling. Idempotent.

symbols.name: stop_watch
symbols.note: Stops poller and joins thread. Idempotent.

symbols.name: _watch_loop
symbols.note: Background loop: polls should_stop, waits on _watch_stop, calls stop_children on trip.

symbols.name: _atomic_write
symbols.note: Delegates to write_text_atomic for atomic write with retry.

claims.text: Why the switch latched, or ``None`` while it has not.
claims.why: Property returns self._reason which is set to reason on latch in should_stop.

claims.text: ``(present, unreadable_reason)``. NOT ``Path.exists()``. ``exists()`` swallows every OSError and answers False, so an ACL that denies us the marker would read as 'no stop was requested' -- the precise fail-open this module exists to avoid. Only ``FileNotFoundError``/``NotADirectoryError`` mean absent; anything else means we could not tell, and could-not-tell is STOP.
claims.why: Code uses os.stat and catches FileNotFoundError/NotADirectoryError to return (False, None); other OSError returns (True, reason); success returns (True, None).

claims.text: Read the permit from disk. Never raises; defaults to stopped. Every early return below is a STOP. There is exactly one ``running`` exit, and it is reached only after the token was positively read and no stop marker was found.
claims.why: All early returns are halt() with stopped=True. The final return is SwitchState(True, ...). No raise in code.

claims.text: True once, then True forever. NEVER raises, and NEVER returns False because something went wrong. The never-raises property is not politeness. ... any internal failure here latches STOP instead of escaping.
claims.why: If read_state raises, caught by BaseException and returns stopped=True, reason set. Once latched, returns True. No raise.

claims.text: Block until the watcher latches. Only meaningful under :meth:`watch`.
claims.why: Code calls self._event.wait(timeout). The claim about watcher latching is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Raise :class:`LoopHalted` if the loop must not proceed. Call this immediately before anything that costs money or writes: it is the enforcement point for the 'no new spend after the latch' bound.
claims.why: Code raises LoopHalted if should_stop returns True.

claims.text: Register a :class:`~daedalus.spine.cancel.ManagedProcess` to reap. Returns its argument so it can wrap a constructor inline. Tracking is belt-and-braces: :func:`~daedalus.spine.cancel.cancel_all_managed` already sweeps every live ``ManagedProcess`` in this interpreter, which is what stops a gate child whose loop driver forgot to thread the cancel token through.
claims.why: Code appends managed to self._tracked and returns managed. The sweep claim is uncheckable but the registration is correct.

claims.text: Cancel every tracked tree, and (by default) every live managed tree. Returns the cancel results. Idempotent per trip; a second call after everything is already dead is cheap and harmless.
claims.why: Code iterates tracked, calls proc.cancel, and if self._sweep_managed calls cancel_all_managed. Idempotent due to lock and children_stopped flag.

claims.text: Start the background poller. Idempotent. A DAEMON thread that exits on the first trip: a watcher that outlives its trip is the 'stale watcher still running old code' failure this repo has already paid for once.
claims.why: Code checks if watcher exists and alive; if so returns. Creates daemon thread. The thread exits in _watch_loop when should_stop returns True.

claims.text: Stop the poller and join it. Idempotent; safe after a trip.
claims.why: Sets _watch_stop, gets watcher, sets to None, joins if not current thread.
Returns _WatchScope(self). The class _WatchScope is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Replace ``target`` atomically, retrying a Windows sharing conflict. MEASURED, and the reason this retry exists: on win32 a poller reading the permit holds it open WITHOUT ``FILE_SHARE_DELETE`` (CPython's ``open()`` offers no way to ask for it), so ``MoveFileEx`` over it returns ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED. With a 50 ms poll that raced often enough to break the operator's own stop command -- i.e. the kill switch could fail to engage precisely because something was watching it. The window is one ``read_bytes`` of a <1 KiB file, so a bounded retry closes it; the caller decides what an exhausted retry means. This is where that retry was first measured and written. It now delegates to :mod:`daedalus.atomic`, which is this same loop lifted so the four other publishers that documented themselves as atomic and omitted it (``arch_memory.save``, ``shift._write_atomic``, ``file_bridge._write_json_atomic``, ``loop.LoopLedger.save``) share one implementation instead of four divergent copies. Behaviour here is unchanged: same temp-sibling scheme, same bounded retry, same raise on an exhausted deadline.
claims.why: Code calls write_text_atomic(target, text, retry_s=retry_s). The claim about delegation and retry is correct per code. The historical context is uncheckable but the current behavior matches.

observations.what: _marker_present uses os.stat, not Path.exists, to avoid swallowing OSError. This is explicitly documented and implemented.
read_state has multiple early returns that all call halt() with stopped=True. The only non-halt return is the final one with stopped=True (armed).
should_stop catches BaseException to ensure it never raises. This is a broad catch, but documented.
The _watch_loop comment describes a race condition and the use of cooperative_grace_s to mitigate it. This claim cannot be verified in this chunk.
_atomic_write delegates to write_text_atomic. The import is not shown, but the call is present.
